method.method_draft: Use the general recurrence implied by the rule on a cycle: if consecutive circle values are ..., a, b, c, ..., then b = a + c, so c = b - a. Therefore any two consecutive values determine the whole sequence, and the recurrence repeats every 6 positions: a, b, b-a, -a, -b, a-b, a, b, .... In an 8-circle cycle, the same sequence must also repeat every 8 positions. A sequence with both period 6 and period 8 must have period gcd(6,8)=2, so all circles in positions of the same parity around the cycle must have the same value. In the image, the circles containing 3 and 5 are separated by exactly one circle at the top, so they lie in the same parity class of the 8-cycle. Thus they would have to be equal, but 3 ≠ 5. Therefore the diagram is inconsistent before even choosing '?', so the answer is no solution.
